2e25aa95-7fb0-4804-8319-219cb7981c63.cell_value: Growing Tavrin Squash. Tavrin is a compact winter squash suited to raised beds and large containers. Sow seeds indoors in small pots about four weeks before the last expected frost, pressing each seed 2 cm deep. Keep the pots somewhere bright at around 20 degrees Celsius. Seeds usually sprout within 7 to 10 days. Once the risk of frost has passed, plant the seedlings outside, leaving 60 cm between plants. Tavrin likes rich soil, so dig in a bucket of compost for each plant before planting. Water twice a week at the base of the plant rather than over the leaves, and give extra water in dry spells. A layer of straw under the developing fruit keeps it off damp soil. Each plant usually carries three to five fruits. Pinch out the growing tip once the main stem reaches about 1.5 metres.

2e25aa95-7fb0-4804-8319-219cb7981c63.cell_value: How Dew Forms. Air always contains some water vapour, and the amount it can hold depends on its temperature: the cooler the air, the less vapour it can hold. After sunset, grass, leaves and car roofs lose heat by radiating it up into the sky. On clear nights this cooling is strong, because there are no clouds to send heat back down. As a surface cools, it chills the thin layer of air touching it. When that air reaches its dew point, the temperature at which it can no longer hold all of its water vapour, the extra vapour condenses into droplets on the surface. Still air helps, because wind mixes the cooled layer with the air above. This is why dew is most common on calm, clear nights and is often seen in the early morning. If the dew point is below freezing, the vapour turns straight into ice crystals instead, which we call frost.

2e25aa95-7fb0-4804-8319-219cb7981c63.cell_value: Pruning Lavender. Lavender stays bushy and flowers well for longer if it is pruned once a year. The best time is late summer, straight after the flowers have faded. Use clean, sharp shears and cut back the soft green stems by about two thirds, but always leave at least two or three sets of leaves on each stem. Avoid cutting into the bare, woody base of the plant, because old wood rarely grows new shoots. Shape the plant into a neat mound so that rain runs off it. A light tidy in spring, removing any frost-damaged tips, is fine, but do not prune hard at that time. Young plants can be pinched back lightly in their first spring to encourage branching. 2e25aa95-7fb0-4804-8319-219cb7981c63.cell_value: How a Rainbow Forms. A rainbow appears when sunlight shines on falling raindrops while the sun is behind the viewer. As light enters each drop, it slows down and bends, a process called refraction. Different colours bend by slightly different amounts, so white light spreads out into a band of colours. The light then reflects off the back of the drop and bends again as it leaves. Each drop sends one colour to your eye, depending on its angle, which is why the colours sit in rings. In the main rainbow, red is on the outside and violet is on the inside. A rainbow can only be seen when the sun is lower than about 42 degrees above the horizon, which is why rainbows are most common in the early morning and late afternoon. Sometimes a fainter second bow appears outside the first, with its colours in reverse order.

2e25aa95-7fb0-4804-8319-219cb7981c63.cell_value: Why Leaves Change Colour in Autumn. Leaves are green in summer because they are full of chlorophyll, the pigment plants use to capture sunlight and make food. Leaves also contain yellow and orange pigments called carotenoids, but in summer the chlorophyll hides them. As autumn days get shorter and nights get cooler, many trees stop making chlorophyll. The green fades, and the yellow and orange carotenoids that were there all along show through. Red and purple colours come from a different group of pigments, called anthocyanins. Unlike carotenoids, these are made fresh in autumn, mostly in leaves that get bright sunshine during the day and cool, but not freezing, nights. This is why the reds are often strongest after a run of sunny days. Eventually a layer of cells forms where the leaf stalk joins the branch, and the leaf falls.

To descale, dissolve 25 g of citric acid in 1 litre of cold water and pour the mix into the kettle up to the 1.0 litre mark. Bring it to the boil, switch the kettle off and leave the solution to stand for 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, empty the kettle, rinse it twice with fresh water, then boil one full kettle of clean water and pour it away before normal use. Wipe the outside with a damp cloth only; never put the kettle or its base in water or in a dishwasher. If flakes remain, repeat the process once.

2e25aa95-7fb0-4804-8319-219cb7981c63.cell_value: Hail forms inside tall thunderstorm clouds called cumulonimbus, where strong updrafts carry raindrops high above the freezing level. There the drops freeze into small ice pellets. As a pellet falls, it collects a coat of supercooled water, which freezes onto it; if an updraft lifts it again, another layer is added. Cutting a large hailstone in half often shows rings, much like the layers of an onion, which record each trip through the cloud. A hailstone falls to the ground when it becomes too heavy for the updraft to hold up. Most hailstones are smaller than 2 cm across, but stronger updrafts can support larger stones. Hail is most common in late spring and summer, when heated ground air drives the strongest updrafts, and it rarely falls in winter.

2e25aa95-7fb0-4804-8319-219cb7981c63.cell_value: Requests to the Ferrowline API are rate limited per API key. The Starter plan allows 60 requests per minute and the Team plan allows 600. Each response includes the headers X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset; the last gives the number of seconds until the current window resets. When a key goes over its limit, the API returns status 429 with a Retry-After header. Clients should wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After before trying again, and should back off exponentially if 429 responses keep coming. Bulk endpoints such as /v2/records/batch count as one request but accept at most 500 records per call. Limits apply separately to each key, so several services sharing one key also share one limit.

A heap that is wet and smells sour has too many greens, so add browns; a heap that stays dry and does not heat up needs more greens and a little water. Compost is ready when it is dark and crumbly and smells earthy, usually after six to twelve months.

2e25aa95-7fb0-4804-8319-219cb7981c63.cell_value: A rainbow appears when sunlight shines on falling raindrops while the sun is behind the observer. Light entering a drop slows down and bends, a process called refraction. Because each colour bends by a slightly different amount, white light spreads out into its colours. The light reflects off the back of the drop and bends again as it leaves, so it exits at an angle of about 42 degrees from the direction opposite the sun for red light and about 40 degrees for violet. This is why red is on the outside of the main bow and violet on the inside. A fainter second bow sometimes forms outside the first when light reflects twice inside each drop; its colours are in the reverse order. Rainbows are most often seen in the early morning or late afternoon, when the sun is low.

Keep the sealed area dry for 24 hours, and do not walk on sealed floors for at least three hours.
